findings.title: Feed/remote content is stored as raw HTML and rendered unsanitized
findings.body: Imported content is created with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns the raw string unchanged for that method. The content comes from an RSS/Atom feed (poll_feed.rb, after only CGI.unescapeHTML) or a remote page, and is not sanitized. Any HTML or script in a feed item ends up in cooked and is rendered in the embed view with `raw post.cooked`, which is served in an iframe with X-Frame-Options set to ALLOWALL. This is a stored XSS vector from third-party content, and it also skips the normal Markdown/sanitizing pipeline and the spam checks for these posts.

findings.title: Unescaped feed URL interpolated into HTML attribute and link text
findings.body: The footer is built as I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}") without escaping. The url comes from the feed's link/id field and only has to start with http(s)://. A URL containing a single quote or '>' breaks out of the attribute and injects markup into the stored post body, which is then rendered as raw HTML.

findings.title: Caller's contents string is mutated
findings.body: `contents << ...` appends the footer directly to the string the caller passed in. Callers that reuse the string (for example a retry, or a second import with the same variable) get the footer appended twice and a different content_sha1 each time, which causes spurious revisions.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring match instead of equality
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any message whose origin string appears anywhere inside discourseUrl, not only an exact origin match. Partial matches such as a prefix of the configured host can pass. The check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl for equality with e.origin. The message handler then trusts e.data.height to resize the iframe.

findings.title: Referer interpolated into a JavaScript string without JS escaping
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is placed inside a script block. ERB HTML-escaping does not make a value safe in a JS string context, so a referer containing a quote or backslash can break the script. The referer is also used as the postMessage targetOrigin. If it is missing, the call throws a SyntaxError, and a full URL with a path is passed where an origin is expected. Use a JSON-encoded origin computed on the server.

findings.title: Stray `end if` in template produces an unintended modifier-if
findings.body: The line `<%- end if %>` emits `end if` into the compiled template. Ruby parses `if` as a modifier whose condition is the next statement emitted (the next buffer assignment), so the header's logo link is wrapped in a meaningless conditional. The intent was to close the earlier if/else block with a plain `end`. As written, the template is confusing and the link logic is fragile.

findings.title: One feed item without content aborts the entire feed import
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content element (i.content is nil). The exception propagates out of the `rss.items.each` loop, so every subsequent item in the feed is skipped. Items without a body should be skipped or default to an empty string.

findings.title: Anonymous requests can trigger full feed polls repeatedly
findings.body: retrieve is reached from the anonymous embed/best endpoint. The throttle is keyed on the full embed_url, so each distinct URL on the embeddable host bypasses it. Each new URL then runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, which downloads the entire feed over HTTP with no timeout. An anonymous client can drive unbounded outbound fetches and feed re-parsing by varying query strings.

findings.title: Existing migration changed to force-drop the table
findings.body: The change to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` modifies a migration that has already shipped. With force: true, the table is dropped and recreated whenever this migration runs on a database where the table exists, which destroys any data in top_topics. The original migration should not be edited; a new migration should be added if a change is needed.

findings.title: NOT NULL column with default added to large posts table
findings.body: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to posts on large forums can rewrite the whole table and hold an exclusive lock for the duration, blocking writes. This is worth doing in batches or noting as a deployment risk.

findings.title: Removed --category option without replacement or notice
findings.body: The `category` method_option and its handling were removed from the Disqus import command. Existing invocations that pass --category now fail with an unknown-option error, or the option is silently ignored in other paths. The change also switches import from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which the description does not mention.

findings.title: Test named as 404 but only checks non-success
findings.body: The example is titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' but asserts only `should_not be_success`. Missing required params raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, which is not necessarily a 404. The test neither checks the status code nor covers the actual behavior.
